post.summary: Preview and fence a multi-project release
post.description: Validates the complete dependency graph, exact revisions or artifacts, worker placement, current deployments, environment versions, verification policy, and overlap fences without dispatching work. Independent dependency-ready members form an explicit parallel group. An exact-commit member's `expectedCommitSha` must be the head of its `branch`, and is otherwise refused with `409` `SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED`. A member whose repository credential is held by its Worker (a private GitHub service bound to no GitHub installation, GitLab, or Bitbucket) has its head read by that Worker; a Worker that must be upgraded first fails the preview with `409` `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`, and any other unreadable or moved head with `409` `SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED`. Such a member later fails with `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE` when its Worker holds no credential that can read the repository, `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_PENDING` while a supplied one is still being delivered, `SECRET_RESUBMISSION_REQUIRED` when it must be resubmitted, and `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` when its Worker must be upgraded, with no build dispatched. A member whose environment awaits the confirmation of a recovery move's variables (confirmRecoveryMoveVariables) fails with `VARIABLES_UNRECONCILED`, with no build dispatched.

400.description: Invalid request. `VALIDATION`: the request is not a valid release group, for example a member's `dependsOn` repeats a key, names the member itself or a missing key, or the dependencies form a cycle. `INVALID_BODY` also uses this status.

409.description: Conflict. `SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED`: a member's branch head does not match `expectedCommitSha` or could not be verified, or a member's placement, current deployment or source artifact does not match the request. `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`: a member's Worker must be upgraded to read its branch head (`details.workerId`, `details.requiredCapability`). Other conflicts, such as `SERVICE_OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED`, `WORKER_UNAVAILABLE`, `REPOSITORY_UNAVAILABLE`, `SOURCE_ARTIFACT_NOT_READY` and `PUBLIC_VERIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE`, also use this status.

500.description: Server error. `PREVIEW_UNAVAILABLE`: PostGrip could not sign the preview; try again. `DB_ERROR` also uses this status.

Other conflicts on this route also use this status.

get.description: Reads one page of a project service's build or runtime log. A connected service (`source` `target`) has no logs: `409` `SERVICE_OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED`.

parameters.name: follow
parameters.description: Marks the read as one page of a follow. There is no long poll: the page is answered at once. Send `nextCursor` back after `pollAfterMs` to read the lines that arrived since. On runtime logs, `true` is refused with `409` `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` when an environment's Worker cannot continue from a cursor.

400.description: Invalid request. `INVALID_FILTER`: `kind` is not `build` or `runtime`, `environment` or `deployment` is not an id, or `follow` is not `true` or `false` (`message` says which). `INVALID_CURSOR`: the cursor is not one PostGrip issued, or was issued for another request (other filters, kind or deployment).

404.description: Not found. `SERVICE_NOT_FOUND`: no such service; for a build log, no deployment matches the read yet (`message` `no deployment matches this build log read yet`), for example before the app's first deployment; for a runtime log, no environment (or not the one named) has a Worker and a deployment that ran on it.

409.description: Conflict. `SERVICE_OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED`: a connected service (`source` `target`) has no logs. `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`: an environment's Worker cannot continue a runtime log from a cursor (with `follow=true` or a `cursor`). `SERVICE_ENVIRONMENT_REQUIRED`: the read matches too many environments; name one.

410.description: Gone. `CURSOR_EXPIRED`: the cursor is more than 24 hours old. `CURSOR_GAP`: the lines the cursor points to were removed, the build log changed, or the environments' Worker assignment changed. Read again without `cursor`.

post.summary: Probe a target or deployed service

409.description: Conflict. `SERVICE_AUTHENTICATION_FAILED`: a connected PostgreSQL service answered the Worker but refused its login: the password is wrong (SQLSTATE `28P01`), or the server does not admit the user from the Worker's address (`28000`, for example no `pg_hba.conf` entry). The service's status becomes `degraded`; give the right password with putTargetServiceConnection, or admit the user on the server, then check again with a new Idempotency-Key. `SERVICE_FILE_NOT_FOUND`: a connected SQLite service's file, or its directory, does not exist on its Worker; the Worker never creates a connected file. The service's status becomes `unreachable`; point the service at the right path with updateTargetService, or create the file on the Worker's host, then check again with a new Idempotency-Key. `SQLITE_READ_ONLY`: a connected SQLite service's file opens but does not accept writes on its Worker: the file, or the directory its journal goes in, is read-only to the Worker. The Worker starts a write and rolls it back, so the file is not changed. The service's status becomes `degraded`; make the file and its directory writable to the Worker and check again. `SERVICE_AUTHENTICATION_FAILED` also answers a web, backend, ZVEC or LadybugDB service whose probe was refused with `401` or `403`: its status becomes `degraded`; give the right credential with putTargetServiceConnection's `http` and check again with a new Idempotency-Key. Such a service's check is one bounded `GET` (10 seconds) from its Worker, with the stored credential: of the service's URL on its port (`collections` under it for ZVEC, `health` for LadybugDB), following redirects only to the same scheme, host and port, verifying TLS with the Worker's system roots. Any other answer below `500` is `200` with `status` `ready` and the answer's `httpStatus`; a `5xx`, a timeout or a failed connection is `503 SERVICE_UNREACHABLE` and the status becomes `unreachable`. `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`: the service's Worker cannot check it (a web, backend, ZVEC or LadybugDB service needs `target_http_auth_v1`). `SERVICE_OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED`: the service cannot be checked. Other conflicts on this route also use this status.

get.summary: Resolve a deploy request to an immutable commit
get.description: Resolves a deploy request to an environment and the immutable head commit of its branch, which deployService then confirms as `expectedCommitSha`. For a private GitHub service bound to no GitHub installation, and for GitLab and Bitbucket services, the service's repository credential is held only by its Workers, so the environment's Worker reads the branch head with it and returns only the commit. The preview fails with `409` `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` (with `details.workerId` and `details.requiredCapability: "repository_head_read_v1"`) when that Worker must be upgraded first, `409` `NO_ELIGIBLE_WORKER` when no Worker can read it, and `409` `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE` when the Worker's credential cannot read the repository. The message then names what the target Worker needs: while a supplied credential is being delivered, wait for it; when it awaits resubmission, resubmit it; with none, or one the repository refuses, supply one (or bind the service to a GitHub account). To deploy a commit without reading the branch head, send it to deployService with `namedCommit: true`.

409.description: Conflict. `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE`: PostGrip cannot obtain the credential it needs to read the branch head, or the Worker that holds the service's credential cannot read the repository with it (the message names what the target Worker needs). `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`: the Worker that must read the head does not advertise `repository_head_read_v1` (`details.workerId`, `details.requiredCapability`). `NO_ELIGIBLE_WORKER`: no Worker can read the head. `GITHUB_INSTALLATION_REQUIRED`: the GitHub account the service is bound to is disconnected or unavailable; reconnect it or rebind the service. Other conflicts, such as `SERVICE_OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED` and `SERVICE_ENVIRONMENT_REQUIRED`, also use this status.

502.description: Bad gateway. `REPOSITORY_UNAVAILABLE`: the branch could not be resolved to a commit, because the repository was unreachable, or the repository or branch does not exist or cannot be read. To deploy without reading the branch, use deployService with `namedCommit: true`.

post.summary: Queue a deployment for a confirmed commit
post.description: Queues a deployment of a confirmed commit to one environment. `expectedCommitSha` must equal the branch head previewServiceDeploy resolved (otherwise `409` `SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED`); for a service whose repository credential is held by its Workers, the environment's Worker reads that head. With `namedCommit: true`, `expectedCommitSha` is deployed as given without reading the branch head: it must then be a full 40-character hexadecimal commit SHA (otherwise `400` `VALIDATION`) and is normalized to lowercase, and `branch`, or else the default branch, is recorded unverified. A private GitHub service deploys with the repository credential supplied to the target Worker when that Worker holds one. A deployment never mints an installation token over a supplied credential, including for a service adopted from a GitHub installation; only adoption or rebinding the service moves it back to its installation. The request fails with `409` and queues nothing when the supplied credential cannot be used: `SECRET_RESUBMISSION_REQUIRED` when it awaits resubmission or a re-send of it failed, and `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_PENDING` with `Retry-After` while it is still being delivered, whether the service is bound to no GitHub installation, adopted from one, or bound to one from the console. For a service whose repository credential is held by its Workers, `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE` means the target Worker holds no credential, or one the repository refuses. A Worker that must read the head and does not advertise `repository_head_read_v1` fails the request with `409` `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`, and no Worker able to read it with `409` `NO_ELIGIBLE_WORKER`. None of these refusals consumes the Idempotency-Key: resubmit or supply the credential with putServiceRepositoryCredential (`source-access`), bind the service, wait for the delivery, or upgrade or assign the Worker, then retry the request, with the same key if you like.

400.description: Invalid request. `VALIDATION`: `namedCommit` is set and `expectedCommitSha` is not a full 40-character hexadecimal commit SHA. Other invalid requests, such as `INVALID_BODY` and `INVALID_BRANCH`, also use this status.

409.description: Conflict. These refusals queue nothing and are not stored against the Idempotency-Key, so a retry with the same key runs the request again: `SECRET_RESUBMISSION_REQUIRED`, the target Worker's supplied repository credential awaits resubmission or a re-send of it failed (resubmit it with putServiceRepositoryCredential, `source-access`); `VARIABLES_UNRECONCILED`, the environment was recovery-moved off a lost Worker and its variables await confirmation (supply them on its Worker, then confirmRecoveryMoveVariables; `details.recoveryMoveId`); `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_PENDING`, the Worker's supplied credential is still being delivered (retry after `Retry-After` seconds); `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE`, the Worker that holds the service's credential holds none, or holds one the repository refuses (supply one with putServiceRepositoryCredential, `source-access`, or bind the service); `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`, that Worker must be upgraded to read the branch head (`details.workerId`, `details.requiredCapability`); `NO_ELIGIBLE_WORKER`, no Worker can read the branch head; `WRITE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, a ZVEC or LadybugDB service's starter Compose file write reached the target Worker and its answer was lost, so the file may or may not have been written, and nothing was deployed (a retry rereads the file before it deploys). `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE` is also returned, and stored against the key like other conflicts, when PostGrip cannot obtain the credential it needs to read the branch head. `NO_COMPATIBLE_WORKER`, the environment's Worker cannot take the deployment: it is offline, in maintenance, not trusted, or lacks a capability the deployment needs, such as `build`, or `service_static_host_builds_v1` for a static site (bring it back or assign another Worker); `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`, that Worker must be upgraded before it takes the deployment; `GITHUB_INSTALLATION_REQUIRED`, the GitHub account the service is bound to is disconnected or unavailable (reconnect it or rebind the service). These three are not stored against the Idempotency-Key either. Other conflicts on this route, such as `SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED`, `SERVICE_ENVIRONMENT_REQUIRED`, `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` and `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`, also use this status.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Sent with `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_PENDING` and `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`.

post.description: Connects a database or HTTP service that already runs where the Worker `workerId` can reach it. `metadata.kind` says what it is; omitted, it is `postgresql`. The fields each kind needs: `postgresql` needs `host` and `databaseName`; `sqlite` needs `databaseName`, the database file's path on the Worker, and needs no `host` or `port`; `web`, `backend`, `zvec` and `ladybugdb` need `host`. A missing one is refused with `400` `VALIDATION`. Without `port`, or with `0`, the port is the kind's default: `5432` for `postgresql`, `443` for `web`, `8080` for `backend`, `7000` for `zvec` and `7100` for `ladybugdb`.

Service-Catalog-ETag.description: The tenant's service catalog ETag after this change. Send it as `If-Match` on the next catalog-fenced mutation (`createServiceApp`, `createServiceProject` or `attachTargetService`). A replay with the same Idempotency-Key does not carry it; read the catalog ETag again before the next mutation.

409.description: Conflict. `WORKER_REVOKED`: `workerId` names a revoked Worker (`details.workerId`). Revoked is terminal: enroll a new Worker or replace the revoked one. The refusal is permanent, so a retry with the same Idempotency-Key replays it. A removed or replaced Worker, including one that is also revoked, answers `404` `NOT_FOUND`. `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`: the Worker does not advertise a capability the operation needs (`details.workerId`, `details.requiredCapability`); upgrade the Worker and retry. This refusal is not stored against the Idempotency-Key, so a retry with the same key runs again. Other conflicts on this route also use this status.

Conflict. `TARGET_CREATION_PENDING`: a keyed creation of the target (the console's `POST /api/targets` with an `Idempotency-Key`) is still pending, so the target can't be changed yet. Nothing is changed or queued, and the refusal is not stored against the Idempotency-Key: retry with the same key once the creation settles. `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`: the target's Worker does not advertise a capability the change needs (`details.workerId`, `details.requiredCapability`); this refusal is not stored against the key either. Other conflicts, such as `SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED`, also use this status.

post.description: Repairs one volume of a committed recovery move, fenced by `If-Match` on the record's ETag. Only an `adopt-on-destination` volume whose step is `failed` or `pending`, of an open record whose environment is still on the move's destination, is revised, to `recreate-empty` or `replace-with`. In one transaction it holds the destination as a placement target, ends the destination's adoption operation as `superseded`, abandons the volume's migration and managed-volume records (deleting nothing on any host), binds the new volume (provisioned empty, or the named replacement) and stages its operation. It acts on the record and never re-evaluates whether the original source is lost: a new reassignment cannot repair the move, because its source, the destination, is live and its pending adoption refuses an ordinary reassignment. Refusals write nothing.

409.description: Conflict. `RECOVERY_STEP_NOT_REVISABLE`: the volume is not an `adopt-on-destination` volume whose step is `failed` or `pending`, or the record is closed (`details.disposition`, `details.stepState`, `details.closed`). `SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED`: the environment is no longer on the move's destination. `WORKER_REVOKED`: the destination was revoked after the move (`details.workerId`); a destination removed or replaced since answers `404` `NOT_FOUND`. `WORKER_UNAVAILABLE`: the destination has lost its session and cannot accept the staged operation (`details.workerId`); recovery-move the environment off it first. This refusal is not stored against the Idempotency-Key, so a retry with the same key runs again. `VOLUME_BINDING_CONFLICT`: the replacement is not available on the destination. Other conflicts on this route also use this status.

post.description: Confirms that the variables the environment's Worker now holds are the complete set, after a recovery move off a lost Worker. Variable values lived only on the lost source, so the move restores none: it records the variables the control plane knows of (the record's `variables.knownVariables`), creates each `resubmissionRequired` one on the destination with an empty value, and refuses every deployment of the environment as `409 VARIABLES_UNRECONCILED` until this confirmation. Supply every value on the environment's Worker first (through the Service API or the console); any other variable the environment needs must be created too, since the known inventory may be incomplete. `If-Match` is the variable collection ETag of the Worker the environment is on (the move's destination, or the Worker a later live reassignment relayed the set to), read from its masked variable collection, so you confirm exactly the set you read. In one transaction it clears the environment's mark, marks the record's variables `confirmed` and advances the record's version, and it is audited with every confirmed variable name. Refusals write nothing.

A change that points a `gitlab` or `bitbucket` app at another repository reads that repository's visibility anonymously first, as creation does: PostGrip accepts no source credential for those providers yet, so a private repository, or one that does not exist, is refused with `422` `REPOSITORY_NOT_PUBLIC` (`details.provider`), and a visibility the provider does not answer with `503` `REPOSITORY_VISIBILITY_UNAVAILABLE`.

post.description: Refreshes the repository credential on the service's assigned Workers. `webhook-signing` generates a new webhook signing secret. `source-access` issues a new token from the GitHub installation the project is bound to and never replaces a supplied credential: a Worker whose credential is supplied is skipped and sent nothing, and its target in the staged configuration operation is `succeeded` with `errorCode` `CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_SUPPLIED`. When no Worker can be refreshed from an installation and at least one was skipped because its credential is supplied, which is every Worker when the project is not bound to an installation, the request fails with `409` `CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_SUPPLIED` and stages no operation. A supplied credential is refreshed by resubmitting it with putServiceRepositoryCredential.

409.description: Conflict. `CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_SUPPLIED`: `credentialKind` is `source-access`, no Worker can be refreshed from a GitHub installation, and at least one Worker's credential is supplied (every Worker's, when the project is not bound to an installation). No configuration operation is staged; resubmit the credential with putServiceRepositoryCredential to refresh it. Other conflicts on this route, such as `SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED` and `SERVICE_OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED`, also use this status.

post.description: Promotes a source deployment's revision to a target environment. A private GitHub service deploys with the repository credential supplied to the target Worker when that Worker holds one. A deployment never mints an installation token over a supplied credential, including for a service adopted from a GitHub installation; only adoption or rebinding the service moves it back to its installation. The request fails with `409` and queues nothing when the supplied credential cannot be used: `SECRET_RESUBMISSION_REQUIRED` when it awaits resubmission or a re-send of it failed, and `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_PENDING` with `Retry-After` while it is still being delivered, whether the service is bound to no GitHub installation, adopted from one, or bound to one from the console. For a private GitHub service bound to no GitHub installation, `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE` means the target Worker holds no supplied credential. None of these three refusals consumes the Idempotency-Key: resubmit or supply the credential with putServiceRepositoryCredential (`source-access`), bind the service, or wait for the delivery, then retry the request, with the same key if you like.

409.description: Conflict. Five refusals queue nothing and are not stored against the Idempotency-Key, so a retry with the same key runs the request again: `SECRET_RESUBMISSION_REQUIRED`, the target Worker's supplied repository credential awaits resubmission or a re-send of it failed (resubmit it with putServiceRepositoryCredential, `source-access`); `VARIABLES_UNRECONCILED`, the environment was recovery-moved off a lost Worker and its variables await confirmation (supply them on its Worker, then confirmRecoveryMoveVariables; `details.recoveryMoveId`); `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_DELIVERY_PENDING`, the Worker's supplied credential is still being delivered (retry after `Retry-After` seconds); `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE`, the service is bound to no GitHub installation and the target Worker holds no supplied credential (supply one with putServiceRepositoryCredential, `source-access`, or bind the service); `WRITE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, a ZVEC or LadybugDB service's starter Compose file write reached the target Worker and its answer was lost, so the file may or may not have been written, and nothing was deployed (a retry rereads the file before it deploys). `NO_COMPATIBLE_WORKER`, the environment's Worker cannot take the deployment: it is offline, in maintenance, not trusted, or lacks a capability the deployment needs, such as `build`, or `service_static_host_builds_v1` for a static site (bring it back or assign another Worker); `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`, that Worker must be upgraded before it takes the deployment; `GITHUB_INSTALLATION_REQUIRED`, the GitHub account the service is bound to is disconnected or unavailable (reconnect it or rebind the service). These three are not stored against the Idempotency-Key either. Other conflicts on this route, such as `SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED`, `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` and `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`, also use this status.

Only a `failed` or `blocked` operation whose `kind` ends in `-delete` (`project-delete`, `environment-delete`, `volume-delete` or `target-delete`) can be abandoned; anything else answers `409` `CONFIGURATION_OPERATION_NOT_ABANDONABLE` with `details.reason` (`not-a-delete`, `state`, or `stack-child` for an operation a configuration stack staged, which its stack retries) and `details.state`. `If-Match` is the operation's `etag`; a change after it was read answers `412` `PRECONDITION_FAILED`. No Worker is contacted. The operation becomes `abandoned` and is never run or retried again. The service is already gone from PostGrip; each Worker whose target did not succeed keeps what it still holds of it: the containers, the Compose file, the environment's variables and secrets, the domain routes, and the volumes with their data. The volumes the delete was removing stop being tracked and are listed in `abandonedVolumes` with the Worker that holds each. A repository credential the delete revoked keeps its own cleanup record, which PostGrip keeps retrying and the console shows on the GitHub account. To clean a Worker up, remove the containers and volumes on its host, or remove the Worker.

With `If-Match` set to the `etag` getServiceComposeFile answered, the file is replaced only if it has not changed since: otherwise `412` `PRECONDITION_FAILED`, and nothing is written. A conditional write needs a Worker with versioned Compose files, the ones whose read answers an `etag`; an older Worker answers `409` `WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`. When the write's answer is lost, `409` `WRITE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`: read the file again before retrying. The new `etag` is only in the answer in hand: a replay of the same Idempotency-Key answers the file without `etag` and with no `ETag` header, so read the file again for its ETag. An `If-Match` that is not one Compose ETag answers `400` `VALIDATION`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Optional: the Compose file's `etag`, as getServiceComposeFile answers it. The file is replaced only while it still has that ETag.

200.description: Successful response. A conditional write answers the file's new `etag`, in `compose.etag` and the `ETag` header; an unconditional one, and a replay of either, answers none.

ETag.description: The Compose file's ETag after a conditional write.

404.description: Not found. `SERVICE_NOT_FOUND`: `serviceId` or `environmentId` is not a UUID, or names no service or environment of the tenant.

delete.description: Deletes the Worker-held Compose override so the next read or deployment can restore generated defaults.

404.description: Not found. `SERVICE_NOT_FOUND`: `serviceId` or `environmentId` is not a UUID, or names no service or environment of the tenant.

get.description: Returns saved non-secret values from the assigned Worker. Secret values are represented only by metadata and are never returned.

Returns traffic telemetry status from every Worker assigned to the project or selected environment. Only an app (a project service) has these; a connected service's id answers `404` `SERVICE_NOT_FOUND`.
Returns bounded traffic time-series and breakdown data from every assigned Worker. Only an app (a project service) has these; a connected service's id answers `404` `SERVICE_NOT_FOUND`.

put.description: Updates project-scoped traffic collection and retention settings on every assigned Worker. Only an app (a project service) has these; a connected service's id answers `404` `SERVICE_NOT_FOUND`.

post.description: Deletes traffic rollups older than the configured retention window on every selected Worker. Only an app (a project service) has these; a connected service's id answers `404` `SERVICE_NOT_FOUND`.
Deletes all project or selected-environment traffic rollups on every selected Worker. Only an app (a project service) has these; a connected service's id answers `404` `SERVICE_NOT_FOUND`.

postgripToken.description: Tenant-scoped PostGrip management token carrying concrete Agent, Worker, and Service grants.

OptionalEnvironment.name: environment
OptionalEnvironment.description: Resolved environment UUID. When omitted, the operation covers every assigned environment in the project.

ReleaseGroupLimit.name: limit
ReleaseGroupLimit.description: Page size. A missing, non-numeric, zero or negative value means 100, and a value above 100 means 100; neither is refused.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Page size. A missing, non-numeric, zero or negative value means 100, and a value above 200 means 200; neither is refused.

ConfigurationOperationLimit.name: limit
ConfigurationOperationLimit.description: Page size. A missing, non-numeric, zero or negative value means 50, and a value above 100 means 100; neither is refused.

GitHubInstallationRef.name: installationRef
GitHubInstallationRef.description: The connected GitHub account (installation) to act through. Required only when the tenant has several active accounts and the request is not otherwise resolved to one.

details.description: Machine-readable context of the refusal. A `400` `INVALID_BODY` from the request body check has `reason`: `body_required`, `body_not_allowed`, `malformed_json`, `not_an_object`, `unknown_field`, `wrong_type`, `invalid_value`, `null_field`, `missing_field` or `empty_field`; and, when one field is at fault, `field`: its JSON name or path, such as `members[0].environmentId`. They never hold a value from the body, and `message` says the same in words.

ServiceReleaseGroupMemberState.description: `dispatching` is reserved: no member is put in that state today, so a client sees a member go from `pending` to `deploying`. A member that is not `required` and fails after it went live stays `failed` while the group runs; when the group succeeds it ends `intervention_required` with `errorCode` `OPTIONAL_MEMBER_FAILED`, which frees its environment for another release, a reassignment or a delete. Its environment may run the failed deployment: check it, and deploy or roll it back.

expectedCommitSha.description: The commit to deploy, with `branch`. It must be the head of `branch`; for a service whose repository credential is held only by its Workers, the member's Worker reads that head.

expectedArtifactIdentity.description: With `sourceDeploymentId`: the source deployment's artifact identity, as previewServicePromotion answers it in `artifactIdentity`.

expectedCurrentDeploymentId.description: The environment's current deployment, as getServiceEnvironment's `currentDeploymentId` gives it. Omit it only when the environment has none: an omitted value is compared as "none", and a mismatch is refused.

reversible.description: Set false for stateful members that must never be silently rolled back. A cutover followed by group failure then reports intervention_required.

errorDetail.description: Safe bounded release detail; Worker errors and secrets are not exposed.

ServiceKind.description: `nodedb` is a legacy kind: existing NodeDB services are still listed, but none can be created (createServiceProject refuses one with `400` `VALIDATION`).

cutoverState.description: The deployment's role in the production cutover lifecycle. A candidate is building but cannot receive traffic, cutover is ready and switching, rollback_candidate is an explicit rollback that is queued or building and cannot receive traffic, rollback_cutover is an explicit rollback whose target is ready and switching, live is the routed deployment, retained is the one last known-good rollback target, historical is a completed deployment whose runtime is not retained, and terminal is an incomplete deployment that is neither routed nor retained.

errorCode.description: Set when `status` is `failed`, and one of a closed set: `BUILD_FAILED` when the build failed (the image build, or a static site's dependency install, build command or missing output directory); `IMAGE_PULL_FAILED` when the Worker could not pull the image the service runs; `HEALTHCHECK_FAILED` when the new container did not accept connections on its port in time, or failed its browser check; `REQUIRED_SECRET_MISSING` when the application could not start because a secret it requires is not set on the environment; `WORKER_LOST` when the Worker stopped reporting on the deployment before it finished, because its lease expired or it reported no progress for 30 minutes; `DEPLOYMENT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` when the deployment stayed `queued` for 30 minutes without its Worker taking it, for example because the Worker was offline or busy; and `DEPLOYMENT_FAILED` for any other failure, a failure an older Worker reported, and a deployment that failed before these codes existed. The build log (listServiceLogs with `kind=build`) says why. A failed deployment is not retried: fix the cause, or bring the Worker back, and deploy again. Clients should treat a code they do not know as `DEPLOYMENT_FAILED`.

errorMessage.description: Set when `status` is `failed`: a fixed PostGrip sentence for `errorCode`, the same for every deployment with that code. It never carries the Worker's or the build's text; `DEPLOYMENT_FAILED` answers `deployment failed`. Read the build log for the detail.

LogList.description: One page of a log: at most `limit` lines and at most 256 KiB of them, so a page with fewer lines than `limit` is not the end. `nextCursor` continues after the page; a follow page with no new lines answers the cursor it was sent.

pollAfterMs.description: How long to wait before reading the next page when this one had no new lines: 2000 milliseconds.

namedCommit.description: Deploy expectedCommitSha as given, without reading the branch head. It must then be a full 40-character hexadecimal commit SHA (otherwise 400 VALIDATION); the branch is recorded unverified.

httpStatus.description: For a web, backend, ZVEC or LadybugDB service's check: the HTTP status the service answered the Worker's probe with. Absent for a database.

kind.description: What the connected service is. Omitted, `postgresql`; an empty string is refused. It decides which of `host`, `port` and `databaseName` attachTargetService needs, and the default `port`.

appId.description: The application this service belongs to: a ServiceApp id, as listServiceApps lists them. The console calls an application a Project. Optional here, although the console always sets one.

host.description: The host the Worker connects to. Required for every kind but `sqlite`.

port.description: The port the Worker connects to. Omitted or `0`: the kind's default, `5432` for `postgresql`, `443` for `web`, `8080` for `backend`, `7000` for `zvec` and `7100` for `ladybugdb`. Not used for `sqlite`.

databaseName.description: The database name for `postgresql`, or the database file's path on the Worker for `sqlite`. Required for both; the HTTP kinds do not need it.

appId.description: The application this service belongs to: a ServiceApp id, as listServiceApps lists them. The console calls an application a Project. Optional here, although the console always sets one.

TargetServiceConnectionRequest.description: Exactly one of `password`, for a PostgreSQL service, or `http`, for a web, backend, ZVEC or LadybugDB service. The secret is delivered to the service's Worker only, in a sealed configuration operation; it is never stored by the control plane, audited or answered. `http` on a PostgreSQL or SQLite service, or `password` on an HTTP service, is `400 VALIDATION`; so is a body with neither ("password is required") or both.

TargetServiceHTTPCredential.description: An HTTP service's credential. `none` clears it, like clearTargetServiceConnection; `basic` takes `username` and `password`; `bearer` takes `token`; `api_key` takes `headerName` and `value`. A field the scheme does not take is refused (`400 VALIDATION`, naming the field, never its value). Sending it needs a Worker that advertises `target_http_auth_v1`: otherwise `409 WORKER_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` with `details.requiredCapability`. The Worker stores it with the same bounded expiry as a password and sends it on the service's check.

username.description: `basic` only. No `:` and no control characters.

token.description: `bearer` only, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. No spaces or control characters.

headerName.description: `api_key` only: the header the key is sent in, an HTTP token. `Host`, `Content-Length`, `Content-Type`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Connection`, `Keep-Alive`, `Upgrade`, `TE`, `Trailer`, `Expect`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `Proxy-Connection` and `Cookie` are refused; `Authorization` is allowed, for a custom scheme such as `Token …`.

value.description: `api_key` only. No control characters, and no spaces at its start or end.

TargetServiceHTTPAuth.description: The scheme of an HTTP service's credential as putTargetServiceConnection last set it, with the username for `basic` and the header name for `api_key`; never a password, token or value.

provider.description: `github`: a GitHub repository read through a connected GitHub account (installation) whose login owns `repoOwner`, or through a `source-access` credential supplied to the Workers with putServiceRepositoryCredential. With neither, a deployment is refused with `409` `REPOSITORY_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE`; a public repository should use `public-github`, which is read without a credential. `gitlab` and `bitbucket`: a public repository on gitlab.com or bitbucket.org, which the Workers read without a credential: PostGrip accepts no source credential for them yet. Creating the app reads the repository's visibility anonymously first: a private repository, or one that does not exist, is refused with `422` `REPOSITORY_NOT_PUBLIC` (`details.provider`), and a visibility the provider does not answer with `503` `REPOSITORY_VISIBILITY_UNAVAILABLE`.

installationRef.description: `github` only: the connected GitHub account (installation) to read the repository through, as listServiceGitHubAccounts lists it. It must be an active account of the organization, else `409` `GITHUB_INSTALLATION_REQUIRED`, whose login owns `repoOwner` (letter case does not matter), else `409` `GITHUB_INSTALLATION_MISMATCH` with `details.installationRef` and `details.login`. Not in the form `github-installation:{id}`: `400` `INVALID_INSTALLATION_REF`; with another provider: `400` `VALIDATION`. Omitted, the app is bound to the one active account whose login owns `repoOwner`, and to none when there is no such account or several. The answer's `repository.bound` and `repository.gitHubInstallationRef` report the binding.

appId.description: The application this service belongs to: a ServiceApp id, as listServiceApps lists them. The console calls an application a Project. Optional here, although the console always sets one.

deploymentMode.description: How the app is built and served. Omitted, `static`: the Worker runs the build on its own host and serves the output directory, which needs a Worker whose `capabilities` include `service_static_host_builds_v1`, reported only by a Worker started with `WORKER_UNSAFE_HOST_BUILDS_ENABLED=true`. `docker` builds and runs a container. A `backend`, `zvec` or `ladybugdb` project, and a `docker` or `dockerfile` framework, always use `docker`: omitted, it is `docker` for them, and `static` is refused with `400` `VALIDATION`.

projectType.description: `web` (the default), `backend`, `zvec` or `ladybugdb`; any other value is refused with `400` `VALIDATION`. A `framework` or `serverType` of `zvec` also makes the project `zvec`. `ladybugdb` is never inferred: a `framework` or `serverType` of `ladybugdb` without `projectType` `ladybugdb` is refused with `400` `VALIDATION`.

serverType.description: For a backend (`projectType` `backend`), the container runtime it names: `docker` or `podman`; any other value is refused with `400` `VALIDATION`. It is recorded only: the Worker builds and runs the backend with its own runtime, Docker unless its host sets `CONTAINER_RUNTIME=podman`, so choose a Worker that runs the runtime you name. ZVEC and LadybugDB services take their `projectType`; for a web app it is stored as given.

defaultWorkerId.description: Eligible project-level Worker override used for future environment placement when assignedWorkerId is omitted.

repository.description: Required, except for a `zvec` or `ladybugdb` project, which is built from its engine's public repository when this is left out: `alibaba/zvec` or `LadybugDB/ladybug`, `public-github`, branch `main`, as the console's templates use. A ZVEC service compiles the repository's ZVEC source; a LadybugDB service installs its pinned release, so its repository supplies only the commit. Either always builds with PostGrip's own Dockerfile and HTTP service, whatever the repository holds. Left out for any other project, the answer is `400` `VALIDATION`.

appId.description: The application this service belongs to: a ServiceApp id, as listServiceApps lists them. The console calls an application a Project. Optional here, although the console always sets one.

deploymentMode.description: As on createServiceProject. A `backend`, `zvec` or `ladybugdb` project, and a `docker` or `dockerfile` framework, always use `docker`: `static` is refused with `400` `VALIDATION`, judged on the project as the update leaves it.

projectType.description: As on createServiceProject. A legacy NodeDB project may keep `nodedb`.

serverType.description: For a backend (`projectType` `backend`), the container runtime it names: `docker` or `podman`; any other value is refused with `400` `VALIDATION`. It is recorded only: the Worker builds and runs the backend with its own runtime, Docker unless its host sets `CONTAINER_RUNTIME=podman`, so choose a Worker that runs the runtime you name. ZVEC and LadybugDB services take their `projectType`; for a web app it is stored as given.

defaultWorkerId.description: Sets the eligible project-level Worker override. This placement change additionally requires services:admin.

clearDefaultWorker.description: Clears the project Worker default so future environments return to automatic placement. Setting this to true additionally requires services:admin.

kind.description: Any other value, including one in another letter case, is refused with `400` `VALIDATION`.

assignedWorkerId.description: Explicit placement override. When omitted, the project default or deterministic automatic placement is used.

buildCommand.description: The command the environment's builds run. Empty or omitted, a web app builds with `npm run build`. A backend app has no default, so its build detects its own command, and a backend environment that stored `npm run build` from an earlier default is built as if it had none. A ZVEC or LadybugDB service ignores it.

outputDir.description: The build output directory. Empty or omitted, a web app uses `dist`. A backend app has no default, and a backend environment that stored `dist` from an earlier default is built as if it had none. A ZVEC or LadybugDB service ignores it.

volumes.description: Worker-scoped ephemeral bind mounts. The server derives tenant/project/environment-scoped storage paths from containerPath; Worker-local paths are never accepted or returned.

buildCommand.description: The command the environment's builds run. Omitted keeps the current one; empty sets the default, `npm run build` for a web app. A backend app has no default, so its build detects its own command, and a backend environment that stored `npm run build` from an earlier default is built as if it had none. A ZVEC or LadybugDB service ignores it.

outputDir.description: The build output directory. Omitted keeps the current one; empty sets the default, `dist` for a web app. A backend app has no default, and a backend environment that stored `dist` from an earlier default is built as if it had none. A ZVEC or LadybugDB service ignores it.

volumes.description: Replaces the environment's Worker-scoped ephemeral bind mounts. This field requires services:admin.

disposition.description: What becomes of the volume. For a live source (`sourceLost` false in the preview): `retain-source` keeps the source copy, `delete-source` deletes it, `replace-with` binds `replacementVolumeRef` instead and keeps the source copy. For a lost source (a recovery move): `adopt-on-destination` adopts the volume's legacy directory on the destination host under the same `volumeRef`, and is valid only for a volume with `pendingLegacyAdoption`; `recreate-empty` binds a new volume provisioned empty on the destination; `replace-with` binds `replacementVolumeRef`, which must already be available on the destination. Both abandon the source copy: the control plane stops tracking it and deletes nothing on any host. A live-source value for a lost source, or a recovery value for a live source, is `400 VALIDATION`.

replacementVolumeRef.description: Required with `replace-with`, and only with it.

isSecret.description: Whether the variable is secret. Setting it to `false` on a secret variable that has a value is refused (`400 VALIDATION`): the value was stored as a secret and is never shown, so making it non-secret requires a new value. Use `applyServiceVariables` with the variable's existing `variableId`, `isSecret: false` and the new `value` (without `variableId` the apply creates a new variable and fails with `409 SERVICE_STATE_CHANGED`), or clear the value first with `clearServiceVariableValue`. A secret without a value can be made non-secret here.

httpAuth.description: An HTTP service's credential scheme, once putTargetServiceConnection or clearTargetServiceConnection has set it (after a clear, `none`). Absent for a database, and for an HTTP service whose credential was only set in the console, whose own edits do not record it.

snapshotCovered.description: Present for a connected SQLite service named by an absolute path, once its Worker has reported its data directory (`BACKUP_DIR`): `true` when the file is inside that directory, so the Worker's snapshots include it, `false` when they leave it out. It is judged from the path as given; the Worker also follows symlinks when it takes a snapshot, which reports a file it leaves out under `skipped`. Absent for other services: a worker-managed database's volume is in a snapshot when the snapshot settings' `volumesEnabled` is on.

abandonedVolumes.description: The volumes the delete was removing, which PostGrip no longer tracks. Each stays on its Worker with its data.

login.description: The GitHub login of the user or organization the PostGrip GitHub App is installed on; the account reads only that owner's repositories.

installationRef.description: The connected GitHub account to adopt through. Required only when the tenant has several active accounts and the owner of an owner/name repository does not select one.

ServiceAppDeletionResponse.description: Deletion result for a grouping whose attached projects and target services are retained and detached.

bound.description: `true` when the app reads its repository through a connected GitHub account, which `gitHubInstallationRef` names: the account of its adoption, else the one bound when the app was created. `false` for a `github` app bound to no account, which deploys only with a supplied `source-access` credential, and for every other provider. A binding stays when its account is later disconnected; a deployment then answers `409` `GITHUB_INSTALLATION_REQUIRED`.

gitHubInstallationRef.description: The connected GitHub account (installation) the app is bound to, as listServiceGitHubAccounts lists it. Present only when `bound` is `true`.

ServiceAutomaticDeploymentWiring.description: Last reconciled state of push-triggered automatic deployment wiring. Credential presence alone does not imply that the provider can reach or is configured to call PostGrip.

projectType.description: `web`, `backend`, `zvec` or `ladybugdb`, or `nodedb` for a legacy NodeDB service.

reason.description: Stable audit reason for the resolved placement decision.

buildCommand.description: The command the environment's builds run. Empty, a web app builds with `npm run build`. A backend app has no default, so its build detects its own command, and a backend environment that stored `npm run build` from an earlier default is built as if it had none. A ZVEC or LadybugDB service ignores it.

outputDir.description: The build output directory. Empty, a web app uses `dist`. A backend app has no default, and a backend environment that stored `dist` from an earlier default is built as if it had none. A ZVEC or LadybugDB service ignores it.

mountedByDeploymentIds.description: Present on a volume's own removal impact (getServiceVolumeRemovalImpact) while deployments still mount it: the service's current deployments, its deployments in progress, and its previews whose container the Worker has not removed yet, whose mounts include it. A preview is never current and runs until its Worker removes it: it is listed while it is ready, while it is superseded until a newer preview of it is ready, and while it is expired until its cleanup has completed on the Worker. A ready production deployment that is no longer current, such as a retained release, is not listed. They block the removal: deleteServiceVolume answers `409` `VOLUME_MOUNTED` until the volume is detached, the environment deployed again without it, and its previews removed. A project's or an environment's removal impact does not list them, since that removal removes the deployments too.

canonicalDnsDomainIds.description: Canonical DNS domains whose active or recoverable target blocks this removal until it is reconciled.

durableData.description: Whether the resource holds data that outlives a running container: a managed target, a bound managed volume, or a ZVEC or LadybugDB service, whose data is in its Compose volume (`zvec_data` or `ladybugdb_data`) on its Worker. Removal does not delete that Compose volume, whatever `dataDisposition` says: it stays on the Worker until you remove it there, and it is not listed in `volumes`.

pendingLegacyAdoption.description: True when the volume has a legacy volume migration that has not converged; absent otherwise. When the source is lost such a volume can be adopted on the destination (`adopt-on-destination`).

sourceLost.description: The source Worker is lost: removed, replaced, revoked, or offline with a session it no longer has. The move is then a recovery move: the source is never contacted, its volumes take the recovery dispositions, its pending legacy adoptions do not block the move, and its variables are not relayed: `knownVariables` lists the ones the control plane knows of, and the move leaves the environment refusing deployments until confirmRecoveryMoveVariables. The signed `impactHash` covers it, so a source that changes either way before the reassignment invalidates the preview.

knownVariables.description: Only when `sourceLost`: the variables the control plane knows of for the environment, which may be incomplete (a variable created only through the console is not listed). The move creates each `resubmissionRequired` one on the destination with an empty value; supply every value there, and create any variable the list misses, before confirmRecoveryMoveVariables.

isDefault.description: `true` when the Worker stores no runtime log settings for the app and answers its defaults; `updatedAt` is then the time of the read, not of a change. Absent for stored settings.

errorCode.description: Machine-readable code for the target's outcome, normally set when the target failed or is blocked. A `succeeded` target of a `repository-credential-refresh` operation with `CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_SUPPLIED` is a Worker skipped because its `source-access` credential is supplied: it was sent nothing and kept that credential. A `blocked` target of a repository credential put, clear or refresh, a GitHub repository adoption, or a configuration apply with `CREDENTIAL_SUPERSEDED` is a Worker whose credential a newer decision for the same service already owns: this obsolete intent was not delivered, the Worker keeps the newer decision's credential, and nothing needs to be retried. A `succeeded` target of a deletion (an operation whose kind ends in `-delete`) with `WORKER_CLEANUP_SKIPPED` is a Worker that is gone, removed, replaced or revoked: the deletion completed in the control plane and nothing was sent to that Worker. `WORKER_UNAVAILABLE` on a `blocked` target has two meanings. On a repository-credential target it is a live Worker whose delivery attempts were exhausted, recoverable once the Worker is reachable: for a clear or removal target, retry the cleanup; for an issue target (a put, refresh or adoption), make a new credential decision by repeating the put or refresh. On any other target it is a Worker that is gone, removed, replaced or revoked, which no retry can reach. `MANAGED_VOLUME_ADOPTION_FAILED` on a `failed` target of a `legacy-volume-adopt` operation is the Worker refusing to adopt the legacy directory (missing, unreadable or conflicting); it is retried, and a recovery move's step in that state can be repaired with `reviseRecoveryMoveVolume`.

state.description: Terminal states are `succeeded`, `blocked`, `superseded` and `abandoned`; `failed` is retried with backoff. `abandoned`: an administrator ended this stuck delete with abandonServiceConfigurationOperation; what its Workers still held stays there. `superseded`: a recovery move or its repair took over this operation's work (a legacy volume adoption moved to another Worker, or replaced by another disposition); nothing further runs and nothing needs to be retried.

lastErrorCode.description: Machine-readable code of the operation's last failure or block, as on its targets. `CREDENTIAL_SUPERSEDED` means a newer repository credential decision for the same service and Worker (a later put, clear, refresh, adoption or configuration apply) already owns that Worker's credential: this obsolete intent was not delivered, the Worker keeps the newer decision's credential, and nothing needs to be retried.

recoveryMoveId.description: Set only by `reassignServiceEnvironment` when the source was lost: the ID of the recovery move's record (`getRecoveryMove`), which `reviseRecoveryMoveVolume` repairs.

volumeRef.description: The volume the move previewed: the source copy.

boundVolumeRef.description: The volume now bound on the destination: the same volume for `adopt-on-destination`, a new one for `recreate-empty`, the replacement for `replace-with`.

stepState.description: The state of the destination operation that adopts or provisions the volume: `pending` while it waits or runs, `failed` while it is retried (for example `MANAGED_VOLUME_ADOPTION_FAILED` when the destination host cannot adopt the legacy directory), `blocked` when it cannot run, `converged` once done (or when nothing runs, as for `replace-with`).

lastErrorCode.description: The step operation's last target error code.

configurationOperationId.description: The step's configuration operation, when it has one.

ServiceRecoveryMove.description: The durable record of a recovery move off a lost Worker. Repair acts on it rather than on the environment's current Worker. It is `closed` once every volume step has converged.

replacementVolumeRef.description: Required with `replace-with`, and only with it: a volume available on the move's destination.

ServiceRecoveryKnownVariable.description: A variable a recovery move knows of: one the Service API records for the environment. The inventory may be incomplete: a variable created only through the console is not listed.

resubmissionRequired.description: The variable had a value on the lost source, so a value must be supplied again on the destination before confirmRecoveryMoveVariables. On a record, false also for a variable deleted through the Service API since the move.

unverifiedValue.description: Preview only, for a non-secret variable: the value its Configuration document declares. Nothing proves it current (a console edit does not update the document), so it is a suggestion to verify, never restored.

ServiceRecoveryMoveVariables.description: A recovery move's variables. `unreconciled` from the move, while every deployment of the environment is refused as `VARIABLES_UNRECONCILED`, until confirmRecoveryMoveVariables makes them `confirmed`. Absent on a move recorded before variable reconciliation.

confirmedVariableNames.description: Every variable name the environment's Worker held at the confirmed ETag.

outputDir.description: Static build output directory relative to the repository's configured projectPath. Empty values use the imperative default; non-empty values cannot be absolute, resolve to the project workspace root, or traverse parent directories. Static deployments require build in WORKER_CAPABILITIES and WORKER_UNSAFE_HOST_BUILDS_ENABLED=true on the assigned Worker.

deploymentMode.description: Static mode is supported only for web projects whose framework does not require Docker.

allowRemoval.description: Explicitly authorizes removal of stack-owned projects and environments that are absent from the manifest. Requires prune=true.

removalDataDisposition.description: Required when an explicitly removed project or environment has managed volumes. The selected disposition is fenced into the immutable plan.

reason.description: Why the action has its kind. For a repository `.github` action (the GitHub App reconcile) that GitHub planning blocked: `GITHUB_INSTALLATION_SELECTOR_REQUIRED` (several connected GitHub accounts, and neither the project's binding nor the repository owner selects one), `GITHUB_INSTALLATION_REQUIRED` (the selected account is not an active account of the tenant), `GITHUB_PERMISSION_REQUIRED` or `GITHUB_REPOSITORY_NOT_AUTHORIZED`.

lastErrorCode.description: When the operation is `blocked`, the code of its first blocked action (in action order), as on that action's `lastErrorCode`, or `CONFIGURATION_ACTION_BLOCKED` when the action recorded none; `CONFIGURATION_ACTION_FAILED` when it failed. `CREDENTIAL_SUPERSEDED` means a newer repository credential decision for the same service and Worker already owns that Worker's credential: the obsolete intent was not delivered, the Worker keeps the newer decision's credential, and nothing needs to be retried.

Machine-readable code for the action's last failure or block, including the code of the Service operation it staged. `CREDENTIAL_SUPERSEDED` means a newer repository credential decision for the same service and Worker (a later put, clear, refresh, adoption or configuration apply) already owns that Worker's credential: this obsolete intent was not delivered, the Worker keeps the newer decision's credential, and nothing needs to be retried.

ServiceEphemeralVolumeMount.description: Public projection of a Worker-scoped ephemeral mount. Worker-local storage paths are intentionally omitted.

etag.description: The file's Compose ETag, the `If-Match` a conditional putServiceComposeFile takes. Absent from a Worker without versioned Compose files, from an unconditional write's answer, and from a replayed write's answer: PostGrip never stores a Compose ETag.

value.description: Present only for variables explicitly marked non-secret.

ServiceTrafficSettings.description: An app's traffic settings on one Worker. They are kept per app on each Worker, not per environment, and apply to all of the app's environments there; `lastTrimmedAt` and `lastFlushedAt` are likewise the app's last trim and flush on that Worker, including one that selected environments. `updatedAt` is when the settings last changed on that Worker; a trim, flush or compaction does not change it. Each Worker trims the app's traffic older than `retentionDays` at least hourly, whether or not `enabled` is true or requests arrive. A Worker that has no settings for the app answers the defaults, `enabled: true` and `retentionDays: 14`, with the read's time as `updatedAt` and `isDefault: true`.

isDefault.description: `true` when the Worker has no settings for the app, nor for its organization, and answers the defaults; `updatedAt` is then the time of the read, not of a change. Absent for stored settings.

bucketUnit.description: The unit of the `timeSeries` buckets: `minute` for `window` `1h` (5-minute buckets), `hour` for `6h` and `24h`, and `day` for `5d`, `7d` and `30d`.

deletedRows.description: How many of the Worker's per-minute rollup rows were deleted; not a number of requests.
